title: Sparse, Lattice, and Dense Regimes of Sample-Extrema Clipping Grids for Treated Quantile Effects
banked_reason: The proved positive result concerns a publicly truncated critical window under the exact uniform-X, quadratic-propensity model, not the unfiltered minimum-to-maximum bootstrap-MSE procedure; self-localization of that procedure remains open.
gap_reasons: The proved positive result concerns a publicly truncated critical window under the exact uniform-X, quadratic-propensity model, not the unfiltered minimum-to-maximum bootstrap-MSE procedure; self-localization of that procedure remains open.

The variance-selected interval is honest because calibration controls the entire process and therefore every measurable selector, but the note does not establish selection consistency, convergence to the minimizers of V, or an efficiency gain from variance selection.

The stated fixed public finite clipping-grid, grid-selected QTT deliverable is not proved here: the headline interval selects over the growing random critical set C_n, while the public s-grid appears only in a covariance/reduction clause; define and prove the fixed-grid selection-and-interval theorem or recalibrate the claimed contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage run derived a sparse/lattice/dense sample-extrema grid phase diagram and a functional marked-Poisson and refitted-bootstrap result on a public critical window. The math referee passed, but the decision panel found a substituted fixed-grid headline and missing positioning, while the tier referee capped the delivered package at subfield (6.6 versus the 7.4 field floor). Full-grid bootstrap-MSE self-localization, selection optimality, and positive extension beyond the exact quadratic chart remain open.
tldr: The sample-extrema clipping grid has a complete sparse/lattice/dense phase diagram. When \(L_n-1=o(\log n)\), nonresonant grids miss the \(cn^{-2/3}\) window and resonant grids contribute exactly one random critical knot with limit \(\lambda E^{2/3}\) and hit probability \(h(\lambda)\). At \(L_n/\log n\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), the log critical grid converges along each congruence phase to a randomly shifted lattice of spacing \(2/\kappa\). Only the dense regime \(L_n/\log n\to\infty\) resolves the continuum. There the fully refitted \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap consistently estimates the continuous marked-Poisson law, and simultaneous calibration yields a connected \(90\%\) interval of uniformly \(O(n^{-1/3})\) expected length, including exact ties and totalized exceptional branches.
gap: The closest paper proposes a sample-extrema exponential grid but proves limits only for theoretically specified truncation sequences. It does not characterize the arithmetic fixed-grid hit law, the dense-grid frontier, or the interpolation and quadrature errors created by using the same data to set random endpoints.
fill: The project proves the three-clause fixed- and growing-grid theorem, totalizes every original-sample and bootstrap branch, controls pathwise interpolation and random-endpoint quadrature separately, establishes the functional marked-Poisson law and fully refitted conditional Wasserstein transfer, and delivers a simultaneous selected-QTT interval. The public deterministic finite-grid package is recovered exactly, while self-localization over the unfiltered full grid remains open.
